competition: Bulgarian National Mathematical Olympiad, senior national round, common paper for grades 9–12
source_review_scope: Every AoPS statement was read with LaTeX image alternative text. All six numbered statements and both day headings were present in every year. No essential non-formula statement figure was present. English wording normalized without changing conditions. Area notation explicitly defined in 2023 P4. This is source fidelity review, not independent solution certification or whole-bank verification.

reviews.reviewed_statement: A white equilateral triangle $T$ of side length $2022$ is divided by lines parallel to its sides into equilateral triangles of side length $1$, called cells. Two cells are adjacent if they have a common vertex. Ivan colours some cells black. Without knowing which cells are black, Peter chooses a set $S$ of cells, and Ivan tells him the parity of the number of black cells in $S$. From this information Peter can determine the parity of the number of pairs of adjacent cells of different colours. Find all possible cardinalities of $S$ for which this is possible, regardless of how Ivan colours the cells.

Let $ABC$ be an acute triangle and $M$ the midpoint of $AB$. A circle through $B$ and $C$ meets the segments $CM$ and $BM$ again at $P$ and $Q$, respectively. Let $K$ be the reflection of $P$ in $M$. The circumcircles of $AKM$ and $CQM$ meet again at $X$, and the circumcircles of $AMC$ and $KMQ$ meet again at $Y$. The segments $BP$ and $CQ$ meet at $T$. Prove that $MT$ is tangent to the circumcircle of $MXY$.
Let $x>y>2022$ be positive integers such that $xy+x+y$ is a perfect square. Is it possible that, for every integer $z$ in $[x+3y+1,3x+y+1]$, the numbers $x+y+z$ and $x^2+xy+y^2$ are not coprime?

Let $n\ge4$ be an integer and let $x_1,\ldots,x_n,x_{n+1},x_{n+2}$ be real numbers with $x_{n+1}=x_1$ and $x_{n+2}=x_2$. Suppose there is a real number $a>0$ such that $$x_i^2=a+x_{i+1}x_{i+2}\qquad(1\le i\le n).$$ Prove that at least two of $x_1,\ldots,x_n$ are negative.

Let $ABC$ be an isosceles triangle with $AB=4$ and $BC=CA=6$. Points $X_1,X_2,\ldots$ occur consecutively on $AB$ so that $AX_1,X_1X_2,X_2X_3,\ldots$ form a geometric progression with first term $3$ and ratio $1/4$. Points $Y_1,Y_2,\ldots$ occur consecutively on $CB$ so that $CY_1,Y_1Y_2,Y_2Y_3,\ldots$ form a geometric progression with first term $3$ and ratio $1/2$. Points $Z_1,Z_2,\ldots$ occur consecutively on $AC$ so that $AZ_1,Z_1Z_2,Z_2Z_3,\ldots$ form a geometric progression with first term $3$ and ratio $1/2$. Find all triples of positive integers $(a,b,c)$ for which $AY_a$, $BZ_b$, and $CX_c$ are concurrent.

Let $n\ge2$ be an integer. Sets $A_1,\ldots,A_n$ and $B_1,\ldots,B_n$ of positive integers satisfy $A_i\cap B_j\ne\varnothing$ for every $i,j$, and $A_i\cap A_j=B_i\cap B_j=\varnothing$ whenever $i\ne j$. Arrange the elements of each set in descending order and calculate the differences between consecutive elements. Find the least possible value of the greatest of all these differences.

Let $G$ be a graph on $n\ge6$ vertices, each of degree at least $3$. If $C_1,\ldots,C_k$ are all the cycles in $G$, determine all possible values of $\gcd(|C_1|,\ldots,|C_k|)$, where $|C|$ denotes the number of vertices in a cycle $C$.

Let $ABC$ be an acute triangle. Its excircles touch the segments $BC$, $CA$, and $AB$ at $A_1$, $B_1$, and $C_1$, respectively. Let $O_A$, $O_B$, and $O_C$ be the circumcentres of $AB_1C_1$, $BC_1A_1$, and $CA_1B_1$, respectively. Prove that the lines through $O_A$, $O_B$, and $O_C$, respectively parallel to the internal bisectors of angles $A$, $B$, and $C$, are concurrent.

Let $f(x)$ be a polynomial with positive integer coefficients. For every positive integer $n$, choose positive integers $a_1^{(n)},\ldots,a_n^{(n)}$ with pairwise distinct residues modulo $n$, and put $$g(n)=\sum_{i=1}^n f\bigl(a_i^{(n)}\bigr).$$ Prove that there is a constant $M$ such that $\gcd(m,g(m))>2023^{2023}$ for every integer $m>M$.

Let $ABCD$ be a convex quadrilateral, and let $S_{ABM}$, $S_{CDM}$, and $S_{ABCD}$ denote the areas of the indicated figures. Prove that there is a unique point $M$ on side $AD$ satisfying $$\sqrt{S_{ABM}}+\sqrt{S_{CDM}}=\sqrt{S_{ABCD}}$$ if and only if $AB\parallel CD$.

For every positive integer $n$, determine the least possible value of $$|x_1|+|x_1-x_2|+|x_1+x_2-x_3|+\cdots+|x_1+\cdots+x_{n-1}-x_n|$$ over real numbers $x_1,\ldots,x_n$ satisfying $|x_1|+\cdots+|x_n|=1$.

In a class of $26$ students, each student receives a mark in each of five subjects, with three possible marks in each subject. Prove that, after $25$ students have received their marks, the last student can be given marks that differ from those of every other student in at least two subjects.

Is it true that, for every integer $n>1$, there is an infinite arithmetic progression $M_n$ of positive integers such that $n^m-1$ is not a perfect power for any $m\in M_n$? A positive integer is a perfect power if it equals $a^b$ for integers $a,b>1$.
Points $M$ and $P$ lie on sides $AB$ and $BC$ of a triangle $ABC$, respectively, with $AM=BC$ and $CP=BM$. The lines $AP$ and $CM$ meet at $O$, and $2\angle AOM=\angle ABC$. Find $\angle ABC$.
Find all functions $f:(0,\infty)\to(0,\infty)$ satisfying $$f\bigl(af(b)+a\bigr)\bigl(f(bf(a))+a\bigr)=1$$ for all positive real numbers $a,b$.

Do there exist nonzero real numbers $a_1,\ldots,a_{2024}$, with $a_{2025}=a_1$, such that $$\sum_{i=1}^{2024}\left(a_i^2+\frac1{a_i^2}\right)+2\sum_{i=1}^{2024}\frac{a_i}{a_{i+1}}+2024=2\sum_{i=1}^{2024}\left(a_i+\frac1{a_i}\right)?$$

Let $m$ be a positive integer and $\mathcal F$ a family of four-element subsets of a set with $5^m$ elements. The intersection of any two sets in $\mathcal F$ never has exactly two elements. Find the maximum possible value of $|\mathcal F|$.

Let $ABC$ be a triangle and let a circle $\omega$ with centre $I$ touch sides $AB$ and $AC$ and meet side $BC$ at $X$ and $Y$. The line through $I$ perpendicular to $BC$ meets the line through $A$ parallel to $BC$ at $Z$. Prove that the circumcircles of $XYZ$ and $ABC$ are tangent.
Determine all infinite sequences $a_1,a_2,\ldots$ of real numbers such that $$a_{m^2+m+n}=a_m^2+a_m+a_n$$ for all positive integers $m,n$.

Exactly $n$ cells of an $n\times n$ square grid are black, and the remaining cells are white. The cost of a colouring is the minimum number of white cells that must be recoloured black so that any two black cells can be joined by a sequence of black cells in which consecutive cells share a side. Let $f(n)$ be the maximum cost over all initial colourings with exactly $n$ black cells. Determine a constant $\alpha$ such that $$\frac13 n^\alpha\le f(n)\le3n^\alpha$$ for every integer $n\ge100$.

Let $P(x)$ be a nonconstant monic polynomial with integer coefficients, and let $a_1,a_2,\ldots$ be an infinite sequence of positive integers. Prove that infinitely many primes each divide at least one term of the sequence $P(n)^{a_n}+1$.

Let $ABC$ be an acute triangle with $AB<AC$, midpoint $M$ of $BC$, altitude $AD$ with $D\in BC$, and orthocentre $H$. A circle through $B$ and $D$ is tangent to line $AB$ and meets the circumcircle of $ABC$ again at $Q$. The circumcircle of $QDH$ meets line $BC$ again at $P$. Prove that $MH\perp AP$.
Let $n$ be a positive integer. Prove that there is a positive integer $a$ such that exactly $\lfloor n/4\rfloor$ of the integers $a+1,a+2,\ldots,a+n$ are squarefree.

Let $X_0,X_1,\ldots,X_{n-1}$ be $n\ge2$ points in the plane, and let $r>0$. Alice constructs a connected graph with these vertices and assigns nonnegative real numbers $r_0,\ldots,r_{n-1}$ to them with $\sum_{i=0}^{n-1}r_i=1$. Bob then chooses a sequence of distinct vertices $X_{i_0}=X_0,X_{i_1},\ldots,X_{i_k}$, with $k\ge0$, in which each consecutive pair is joined by an edge. Bob wins if $$\frac1{k+1}\sum_{j=0}^k r_{i_j}\ge r;$$ otherwise Alice wins. In terms of $n$, determine the largest $r$ for which Bob has a winning strategy.

Let $N$ be a positive integer. There are coins of distinct positive integer denominations $a_1,\ldots,a_N$, with exactly $i$ coins of denomination $a_i$ for each $i=1,\ldots,N$. In terms of $N$, determine the largest integer $S$ for which the denominations can be chosen so that every integer from $1$ to $S$ is a sum of one or more of the coins.
Let $n\ge2$ be an integer. Real numbers $a,b$ satisfy $a(b-1)^n+b(a-1)^n=0$. Determine the maximum possible value of $ab$.
Let $a>1$ be an integer and $p>2$ a prime. Determine the remainder of $$(a-1)(a^2-1)\cdots(a^{p-1}-1)$$ upon division by $1+a+\cdots+a^{p-1}$.

Let $ABC$ be a triangle with circumcircle $\Gamma$. A circle $\Omega$ through $B$ and $C$ meets sides $AB$ and $AC$ again at $D$ and $E$, respectively. Let $F$ lie on the smaller arc $DE$ of $\Omega$, and let $\omega$ be the circle through $A$ and $F$ tangent to $\Omega$. Prove that $\omega$ is tangent to $\Gamma$ if and only if line $AF$ bisects $\angle DFE$.

Let $(a_n)_{n\ge1}$ be a strictly increasing sequence of positive integers. Suppose there is an integer $m$ such that $a_{i+1}-a_i<m$ for all $i\ge1$. Prove that there are pairwise distinct indices $p,q,r,s$ such that $a_pa_q=a_ra_s$.

In Baron Munchausen's country there are $2^n$ cities numbered $0,1,\ldots,2^n-1$. Cities numbered $a$ and $b$ are friendly if their binary representations differ in exactly one digit. For example, when $n=3$, cities $0$ and $4$ are friendly, as are cities $5$ and $7$. Between each pair of friendly cities there are two one-way roads, one in each direction. Each road has a category, an integer from $1$ to $n$. At each city, all outgoing roads have distinct categories, while all incoming roads have the same category. Find all $n$ for which this is possible.
